title: Serial Buses: UART, SPI, I2C and CAN

contract.reader: A firmware developer who has to bring up a sensor, memory or controller link on a microcontroller and choose between the four common serial links
contract.problem: Knowing how each link frames, clocks, addresses and checks data, and computing the numbers that make a link work or fail (baud error, transfer time, pull-up value, CAN frame time and bus load)
contract.outcome: Compute UART divider error against the tolerance budget; set an SPI mode from a datasheet; size I2C pull-ups from rise time and sink current; follow CAN arbitration bit by bit; compute worst-case CAN frame time and bus load; choose a bus from the comparison table
contract.contribution: One frame of six questions applied to all four links, worked numbers from the series running examples, and a runnable CAN frame builder with CRC and bit stuffing verified against the standard CRC check value
contract.evidence: Worked arithmetic; one Python program with real output; NXP UM10204 rev. 7.0, ISO 11898-1:2015 and 11898-2:2016, Bosch CAN 2.0, TIA-232-F, TIA-485-A, Davis et al. (2007), Di Natale et al. (2012), Horowitz and Hill (2015)
contract.limitations: Classical CAN and CAN FD as in the cited editions; illustrative delays in the bus-length model; High-speed and Ultra Fast-mode I2C only mentioned; no timing waveforms

findings.location: Section 2.2 UART tolerance display equation (mobile-light-09, mobile-dark-09); Section 5.5 C_m equation (mobile-light-34)
findings.problem: At 360 px the tolerance equation is cut right after '= 5', so a phone reader sees |Delta| < 0.5/9.5 = 5 instead of 5.26 %; the C_m equation loses its closing bracket and t_bit
findings.whyItMatters: 5.26 % is the result of the section, the budget against which the divider errors and Exercise 1 are judged; cut at the result, a correct derivation reads as wrong
findings.action: Split the tolerance equation over two lines (aligned) and break the C_m equation after the + 13 + term so both fit at 360 px
findings.acceptance: On new captures at 360 px, light and dark, 5.26 % is visible without sideways scrolling and the C_m equation shows t_bit

findings.problem: No caption; at 360 px the 'data bytes, ACK, last NACK' and STOP boxes are off-screen with no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: The end of the transaction is exactly what the phone reader does not see
findings.action: Add a caption and a top-to-bottom layout, or rely on the site-level scroll cue
findings.acceptance: facts.json reports 0 SVG figures without a title, and at 360 px all five steps are visible or a scroll cue shows

findings.problem: The bit-sampling point, SPI clock edges and START/STOP conditions are given only in prose and tables, without the timing waveforms the topic is normally taught with
findings.whyItMatters: A reader matching a logic-analyzer trace has nothing to compare it with; Exercise 3 is easier with the four SPI waveforms in view
findings.action: Add up to three generated, captioned inline-SVG timing diagrams (8N1 frame with sample points; SPI CPOL/CPHA; I2C START, data bit, ACK, STOP)
findings.acceptance: The live page shows captioned timing diagrams for UART, SPI and I2C, legible at 360 px in light and dark mode

findings.location: Section 2.4 and Sections 5.1-5.7; Fieldbuses and Industrial Ethernet Sections 2.3 and 4
findings.problem: Both pages explain dominant/recessive bits, arbitration, the worst-case stuffed frame length and the rate-length limit, but neither links the other
findings.whyItMatters: The library presents the same concept twice without connection; a correction to one could miss the other
findings.action: Add a one-sentence cross-reference in each direction and record the pair in the Phase 7 overlap map; no merge
findings.acceptance: Each live page links the other at its CAN section
